question: Who can give the order and directives to the government for the enforcement of fundamental rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court and High Court**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India and High Court** can issue orders and directives to the government to enforce fundamental rights.
 
• **Supreme Court**
 
 
• **Article 32 **of the Constitution of India gives the Supreme Court the power to issue directions, orders, or writs to enforce fundamental rights.
 
• **writs that can be issued include habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto.**
 
• The Supreme Court's jurisdiction is original, meaning an aggrieved citizen can directly go to the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **High Courts**
 
 
• **Article 226** of the Constitution of India gives the High Courts the power to issue prerogative writs to enforce fundamental rights.
 
• **The jurisdiction of the High Courts is concurrent with the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.**
 
• This means that if a citizen's fundamental rights are violated, they can choose to move either the Supreme Court or the High Court direct
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• President:

 
 
• The Indian President is the head of the state.
 
• He is the first citizen of India and is a symbol of the solidarity, unity, and integrity of the nation.
 
• He is a part of the Union Executive along with the Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and Attorney-General of India.
 
• President has the right under the Constitution to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on the question of law.
 
• Once President is elected, he holds office for five years.
 
• He sits in the office even after the completion of five years given no new election has taken place or no new President has been elected till then.
 
• He can also be re-elected and there is no cap on his re-election.
